To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence, awareness and treatment of hypertension in HIV-positive adults attending public sector HIV clinics in the Cape Town, South Africa, was high, but that the proportion of patients with hypertension who had their blood pressure under control, was low.
hypertension is common in young HIV-infected people receiving care in South Africa.

The prevalence, awareness, and treatment of hypertension in HIV infected people attending HIV clinics in South Africa is similar to that in the general population, and is not associated with CD4 count or diagnosed duration of HIV disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevalence, diagnosis and treatment of hypertension, a leading non-communicable chronic disease, among people living with human immunodeficiency (HIV) in the Western Cape province, South Africa.
the prevalence of hypertension in HIV infected people in South Africa.
the burden of hypertension in HIV patients, and how to improve the diagnosis and treatment of this important comorbidity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypertension in HIV infected patients is common in this population, with high prevalence, high awareness, but low treatment and control rates.
hypertension is common in young South Africans with HIV and that the prevalence of hypertension in HIV infected people is comparable to that in the general South African population.
hypertension is a major non-infection comorbidity of HIV infection in young adults in South Africa and that the burden of hypertension is similar in men and in women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hypertension, a major NCD, is common in HIV infected people in care in South Africa, with diagnostic gaps, but with a high proportion of people on antihypertensive therapy and with good control of blood pressure.
we found a high prevalence of hypertension in HIV infected patients attending HIV clinics and that the majority were aware of their hypertension and were on treatment for their hypertension.
we have a high prevalence of hypertension among our patients, and that the majority of them are unaware that they have hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypertension is a common comorbidity in HIV-infected patients in South Africa.
the HIV epidemic in South Africa is now a chronic NCD epidemic.
the burden of NCDs is not limited to the general population and that the integration of NCD and HIV services is needed in South Africa.
